req.title: Login form GET
req.statement: The system shall serve a login form at GET /auth/login.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that GET /auth/login must return an HTTP 2xx response with a login form. I design: (1) a positive EP test verifying exact status 200 and presence of key HTML form elements; (2) a negative NEG test verifying that a wrong HTTP method (POST with no data) still returns a usable response and that a completely wrong path returns 404; (3) a BVA boundary test verifying the exact status code is 200 (not 199, not 201) and that the Content-Type header contains 'text/html'. Together these cover mutation operators: constant-mutation on status codes, string-mutation on response body content, and method-routing mutations.

tests.name: test_login_get_returns_200_with_form
preconditions: Flask app created with TESTING=True and a temporary database
actions: Send GET request to /auth/login via Flask test client
expected: Response body contains b'Log In' or b'login' (case-insensitive form action)
trace: R-FLASKR-007: GET /auth/login -> HTTP 2xx with login form payload
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    init_db()
client = app.test_client()

def test_login_get_returns_200_with_form():
    r = client.get('/auth/login')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert b'<form' in r.data
    assert b'username' in r.data
    assert b'password' in r.data

test_login_get_returns_200_with_form()

actions: Send GET request to /auth/logi (one character short of /auth/login)
Send GET request to /auth/loginx (one character beyond /auth/login)

from flaskr.db import init_db

os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})

tests.name: test_login_get_status_code_exact_boundary
preconditions: Flask app created with TESTING=True and a temporary database
actions: Assert status code is exactly 200 (not 199, not 201, not 302)
Assert response data length is greater than 0
trace: R-FLASKR-007: HTTP 2xx response — BVA pins the exact boundary value 200
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    init_db()
client = app.test_client()

def test_login_get_status_code_exact_boundary():
    r = client.get('/auth/login')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert r.status_code != 199
    assert r.status_code != 201
    assert r.status_code != 302
    content_type = r.headers.get('Content-Type', '')
    assert 'text/html' in content_type
    assert len(r.data) > 0

test_login_get_status_code_exact_boundary()

tests.name: test_login_get_unauthenticated_no_redirect
preconditions: Flask app created with TESTING=True and a temporary database
Client has no session cookie (unauthenticated state)
actions: Send GET /auth/login with follow_redirects=False to detect any unexpected redirect
Verify no redirect occurs (status is 200, not 301/302/303)
expected: Location header is absent or empty (no redirect target)
trace: R-FLASKR-007: unauthenticated client in initial state must receive form, not be redirected
STC: state = unauthenticated -> GET /auth/login -> state stays at login page (200), no transition to redirect
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    init_db()
client = app.test_client()

def test_login_get_unauthenticated_no_redirect():
    r = client.get('/auth/login', follow_redirects=False)
    assert r.status_code == 200
    location = r.headers.get('Location', '')
    assert location == ''
    assert b'<form' in r.data

test_login_get_unauthenticated_no_redirect()
